setup: Create one new plain Mockito unit test class com.redhat.lightwell.service.TransactionServiceFullBalanceTransferTest (no Spring context, no database, no network), following the exact conventions of the existing TransactionServiceTest: annotate the class with @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class); declare @Mock AccountRepository accountRepository, @Mock TransactionRepository transactionRepository, @Mock AuditService auditService, and @InjectMocks TransactionService transactionService. In @BeforeEach, construct all entities in memory: Customer customer = new Customer("John", "Doe", "john@example.com", "555-0101"); Account source = new Account("ACC-000001", AccountType.CHECKING, new BigDecimal("1000.00"), customer); Account target = new Account("ACC-000002", AccountType.SAVINGS, new BigDecimal("250.00"), customer) — two distinct accounts of the same customer, with no dependence on seeded application database IDs. In the single @Test method: (1) stub when(accountRepository.findById(1L)).thenReturn(Optional.of(source)) and when(accountRepository.findById(2L)).thenReturn(Optional.of(target)) using arbitrary locally chosen stub IDs; (2) stub when(accountRepository.save(any(Account.class))).thenAnswer(inv -> inv.getArgument(0)) and when(transactionRepository.save(any(Transaction.class))).thenAnswer(inv -> inv.getArgument(0)) so saved entities are returned unchanged; (3) build TransferRequest request = new TransferRequest(1L, 2L, new BigDecimal("1000.00"), "Full balance transfer") — the amount is exactly equal to the source account's full available balance of 1000.00, the boundary no existing test exercises; (4) execute TransactionResponse response = assertDoesNotThrow(() -> transactionService.transfer(request)) so that an unexpected exception (e.g., InsufficientFundsException from a guard that wrongly treats amount == balance as an overdraw) is reported as an assertion failure rather than escaping as an unhandled test error; (5) after the call, capture the persisted accounts with ArgumentCaptor<Account> via verify(accountRepository, times(2)).save(accountCaptor.capture()) — the service saves source first, then target — and use the captured accounts together with the mutated in-memory source/target instances for the balance assertions.
assertions: Successful completion: the exact-full-balance transfer wrapped in JUnit assertDoesNotThrow completes without throwing any exception — in particular not InsufficientFundsException, which a defective guard that treats amount == balance as overdraw would raise — so the boundary is accepted; the returned TransactionResponse is not null, and any unexpected exception surfaces as an assertion failure rather than an unhandled test error.
Transferred amount: response.getAmount() is equal by comparing to new BigDecimal("1000.00") — exactly the full available balance of the source account is the amount moved.

Source drained (response side): response.getBalanceAfter() is equal by comparing to new BigDecimal("0.00"), since transfer() returns the source-side transaction whose balanceAfter is the source's post-transfer balance.

Persisted source balance: the source Account captured from the first accountRepository.save invocation (equivalently, the mutated in-memory source instance) has getBalance() equal by comparing to new BigDecimal("0.00") — the source ends at exactly zero, never negative and never short-changed.

Persisted target balance: the target Account captured from the second accountRepository.save invocation (equivalently, the mutated in-memory target instance) has getBalance() equal by comparing to new BigDecimal("1250.00") — its original 250.00 plus the transferred 1000.00, so the target receives the identical amount.

Fund conservation: the sum of the post-transfer source and target balances equals the pre-transfer total of 1250.00 (0.00 + 1250.00), proving no funds disappear or appear; equivalently, the amount debited from the source (1000.00 − 0.00) equals the amount credited to the target (1250.00 − 250.00).
Both legs persisted: verify(accountRepository, times(2)).save(any(Account.class)) confirms the updated source and target balances are both written back through the repository.
baseline_expectation: On the original application the test passes. TransactionService.transfer's funds check is `if (source.getBalance().compareTo(request.getAmount()) < 0)`, and 1000.00.compareTo(1000.00) returns 0, so transferring exactly the full available balance is not treated as insufficient funds and no exception is thrown. The service computes sourceNewBalance = 1000.00 − 1000.00 = 0.00 and targetNewBalance = 250.00 + 1000.00 = 1250.00, saves both accounts (source first, then target), saves both TRANSFER transaction rows, logs the audit entries, and returns the source-side response. Consequently: the call completes inside assertDoesNotThrow; response.getAmount() == 1000.00; response.getBalanceAfter() == 0.00; the saved/mutated source balance is 0.00; the saved/mutated target balance is 1250.00; the combined total remains 1250.00; and accountRepository.save is invoked exactly twice.
mutant_expectation: The new test fails on the hidden defective copy while the existing suite alone would remain green, isolating the exact-full-balance boundary. If the defect tightens the funds check to reject equality (e.g., `compareTo(...) <= 0` or otherwise treating balance == amount as overdraw), transfer throws InsufficientFundsException for the full-balance amount and assertDoesNotThrow converts it into an assertion failure. If the defect instead corrupts the arithmetic — source left above or below 0.00, target credited less or more than the amount, the amount subtracted twice, the pre-transfer balance written back, or targetNewBalance computed from the wrong account — the response, persisted-balance, or conservation assertions fail (source != 0.00, target != 1250.00, total != 1250.00, or debited != credited). The existing tests cannot detect such a mutant: shouldTransferSuccessfully moves only 200.00 of a 1000.00 balance (strictly below the boundary) and asserts only source-side response fields; shouldThrowInsufficientFundsOnOverdraw exercises only the withdraw path with amount 2000.00 > balance 1000.00; and no existing test asserts the target account's resulting balance or the balances passed to accountRepository.save. Only this full-balance transfer test distinguishes the defective copy from the baseline.
